text:
Laura: Heads-up — AcmeCorp says ~30-50% of requests are hitting our EU edge even though their client sets X-Client-Region: us-west. They're seeing higher latency and unexpected billing. Repro steps + sample below. Can we confirm router behavior?

Samir: Thanks — can you paste a raw request capture and a couple of request IDs? Any proxy in front of them?

Laura: Proxy in front (api-gw). Sample curl from their dev: 
```
curl -v https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate \\n  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-REDACTED" \\n  -H "X-Client-Region: ,us-west" \\n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\n  -d '{"model":"gpt-4o-mini","input":"hello"}'
```
They say the SDK sets the header as a multi-value string with a leading comma (empty first token).

Jess: I pulled their headers from our overlay logs (request_id=acme-req-20260317-42). We see: 
```
x-client-region: ,us-west
cookie: session=abc123; region=us-west
user-agent: AcmeSDK/2.1
```
RouterBot: route_decision for acme-req-20260317-42 -> tokenized_region_header=[''] -> interpreted_region='' -> fallback_policy -> nearest_pop -> eu1 -> routed.

Samir: Aha — router currently picks the first token in a comma-split header and treats empty string as explicit region (which fails validation and triggers fallback). This matches older behavior when clients sent a single empty value.

Kevin: Quick notes from infra: two immediate remediation options — 1) prefer the last non-empty token when parsing multi-value region headers, or 2) ignore empty tokens during parse. Either is low-risk. Longer-term: add header normalization to reject malformed headers at the proxy edge with a clear 4xx.

Laura: Customer would like a rollback/patch asap — they have production traffic. Which option is fastest to ship and safe?

Kevin: Option 2 (ignore empty tokens) is smallest delta. We can push a router patch to strip empty tokens in header parsing and prefer the first remaining token. I'll scope a canary to us-pop only, then rollout. Estimated 2h dev + 1h canary.

Jess: For immediate help I suggested AcmeCorp add a client-side workaround: ensure SDK does not emit leading commas or add header repair middleware: 
```js
// simple fix in node: 
const region = (header || '').split(',').map(s => s.trim()).filter(Boolean).join(',');
req.setHeader('X-Client-Region', region);
```
They confirmed they can ship that in a hotfix in ~30m.

Samir: Also flagged for billing: some requests billed at eu rates. Finance noted a handful of high-cost calls — I've opened a billing refund request tentatively (ref: BILL-20260317-09).

RouterBot: deploy_patch(stage=canary, target=us-pop) accepted — job 9876 queued.

Laura: I'll reply to the customer with repro steps, mitigation (client hotfix), and ETA for our patch. Tagging them in case they want us to pause traffic to the proxy in the meantime. :thumbsup:

Kevin: After canary validates we'll push global. Also adding a guard in logs to surface "empty-first-region-token" for quick triage.

Jess: Notes for postmortem: root cause = malformed multi-value region header with leading empty token + router parser treating empty-first-token as decisive -> fallback to nearest pop (eu) -> cross-region latency + billing. Action items: short-term header parsing patch, client hotfix guide, billing review, add header validation at edge.

Laura: Thanks team. I'll attach request IDs and the customer's contact in the support ticket.

Samir: ack.
